content: Splicing factor 1 (SF1), also referred to as zinc finger protein 162 (ZFM162), is a protein encoded by the SF1 gene in humans. The SF1 gene plays a critical role in the formation of the bipotential gonad. However, while SF1 expression decreases in the genital ridge of XX mouse embryos, the SF1 gene remains active in the developing testes. SF1, functioning as a transcription factor, is involved in the masculinization of both Leydig cells and Sertoli cells. In Sertoli cells, in conjunction with the SOX9 protein, SF1 enhances the transcription of the anti-Müllerian hormone (AMH). In Leydig cells, SF1 activates the gene responsible for encoding the enzyme that synthesizes the testosterone hormone. SF1 has been demonstrated to interact with several proteins, including the Ewing sarcoma breakpoint region 1, U2AF2, the testis-determining factor, and transcription elongation regulator 1.
